passage:
"Why are you shredding that paratha?" Pankaj asked.
"I'm not."
"You are. What happened?"
Hrithik dropped the piece on his plate. "Nisha was laughing with Dev in the corridor. Like, really laughing. Head back."
"Okay. And?"
"And she never laughs like that with me."
"Did she say anything?"
"No. She waved when she saw me."
"So she waved."
"Bhaiya, you didn't see it. My stomach went all tight. I just knew. She likes him more."
Pankaj raised an eyebrow. "You knew? From one laugh?"
Hrithik opened his mouth, then shut it. "It felt like I knew."
"Feeling like you know and actually knowing are two different things. Now eat your paratha."

qa.q: What did Nisha do when she saw Hrithik?
qa.a: Nisha waved when she saw Hrithik.

qa.q: What does Hrithik's tight stomach tell us about his thinking?
qa.a: It shows the fear came first: Hrithik felt sure Nisha likes Dev more before having any evidence.

qa.q: What could Hrithik do with that tight feeling next time?
qa.a: Hrithik could notice the feeling, remind himself it isn't proof, and simply talk to Nisha normally instead of deciding what she thinks.

qa.q: How does Pankaj see Hrithik's certainty?
qa.a: Pankaj sees that one laugh and a wave aren't proof, and gently points out the gap between feeling sure and knowing.

grounding: Shows a teenage boy seeing his girlfriend laugh with a classmate and jumping to the belief that she likes him more, ahead of any evidence.

passage:
I'm Uday, and I remember the exact moment it started. Last month in the physics lab, Keya, my girlfriend of four months, was paired with Harsha for the pendulum experiment. I was at the next table. She said something, he said something back, and she laughed so hard she had to hold the stand.
My stomach clenched like a fist. Before I'd thought anything through, a sentence was just there in my head: she likes him more than me.
I didn't know what the joke was. I didn't know if it was even funny or just nerves. Keya had told me that same morning she'd been dreading the practical. None of that mattered in that second. The thought was faster than anything I actually knew.
Looking back, I think that was when the jealousy first got its foot in the door.

qa.q: What experiment were Keya and Harsha paired for?
qa.a: They were paired for the pendulum experiment.

qa.q: What thought arrived in Uday's head when Keya laughed?
qa.a: Feeling a jealous clench in his stomach, Uday thought Keya likes Harsha more, a thought that came faster than anything he actually knew.

qa.q: What could Uday have remembered in that moment?
qa.a: That Keya had been dreading the practical, so the laugh might have been nerves, and that a sudden thought isn't evidence.

qa.q: How might Keya have experienced the lab?
qa.a: Keya was probably nervous about the practical and laughing to ease it, with no idea Uday was reading her laugh as a threat.

grounding: Illustrates the first sensed threat of jealousy, when a girlfriend's laugh with a classmate triggers a belief faster than any evidence.

passage:
The school bus had broken down outside Aurangabad on the way back from the science exhibition, and all of Class 10 was stuck on the roadside for an hour.

Imran was handing out water bottles when he saw Farida, his girlfriend of two months, sitting on the milestone with Rehan from the other section. Rehan said something, and Farida threw her head back and laughed, the big laugh Imran thought was only for him.

His stomach clenched like a fist.

She likes him more. The thought arrived fully formed, before he'd even heard what the joke was.

He stood there holding three water bottles, his face hot. He wanted to walk over. He wanted to walk away.

Then Farida looked up, saw him, and waved him over. "Imran! Rehan's telling the story of Sir falling in the pond!"

The fist in his stomach loosened, a little. Not all the way.

qa.q: Where was Farida sitting when Imran saw her?
qa.a: On the milestone, with Rehan from the other section.

qa.q: What was Imran feeling when he saw Farida laugh?
qa.a: He felt a jolt of jealousy and fear, his stomach clenching, as the thought that she liked Rehan more arrived before any evidence.

qa.q: What could Imran remind himself when that thought arrives?
qa.a: That a laugh is not proof of anything, and that he hasn't even heard the joke; he could join them before deciding what it means.

qa.q: How does Farida seem to see the moment?
qa.a: She sees nothing wrong; she is just enjoying a funny story and happily waves Imran over to share it.

grounding: On a broken-down school bus Imran sees his girlfriend laughing with a classmate, and the thought that she likes him more arrives before any evidence.

passage:
The canteen at the school in Pune was loud, but Zubin heard Mehr laugh from across the room.

She was at the table by the window with Tejas from the chess club. Tejas was showing her something on a paper napkin, drawing it, and Mehr was laughing, hand over her mouth.

Zubin's stomach went tight. His sandwich tasted like cardboard.

She likes him more. Tejas is smarter. Tejas is funnier.

He had no evidence. He knew that. He didn't even know what was on the napkin. But the thought had come so fast it felt like a fact.

His friend Aryaman nudged him. "Dude, your face."

"Nothing," Zubin said.

Later, at the gate, Mehr showed him the napkin: a drawing of their maths teacher as a chess knight. "Tejas drew it. Isn't it hilarious?"

Zubin laughed. It came out a little too loud.

qa.q: What was drawn on the napkin?
qa.a: Their maths teacher as a chess knight.

qa.q: What does Zubin's too-loud laugh at the gate suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he still feels uneasy and a bit ashamed, the jealousy not fully gone even after learning it was harmless.

qa.q: What small step could help Zubin next time?
qa.a: Notice that the thought is not a fact, take a breath, and wait to find out what's going on before reacting.

qa.q: How might Mehr feel if she knew about Zubin's thought?
qa.a: She might be surprised and a little hurt that a joke made him doubt her.

grounding: Zubin sees his girlfriend laughing with a classmate and feels his stomach tighten as the thought that she prefers him arrives faster than evidence.

passage:
"Mapuia, why are you so quiet? You've been staring at your girlfriend for five minutes."

"I'm not staring, Zosang."

"You are. What happened?"

"Look at Lalremsiami. With Lalrinfela."

"They're doing the project together. Ma'am paired them."

"She laughed at his joke. She never laughs like that with me."

"Didn't she laugh at your joke yesterday? At lunch?"

"That was different."

"How?"

"I don't know. It just... she likes him more. I can tell."

"You can tell from one laugh?"

"...My stomach went weird, okay?"

"Your stomach went weird because you care. That's not proof."

"Then why does it feel like proof?"

"Because feelings are fast. Facts are slow. Wait for the facts."

qa.q: Why are Lalremsiami and Lalrinfela working together?
qa.a: They're doing the project together because Ma'am paired them.

qa.q: What does Mapuia mean by saying that stomach "went weird"?
qa.a: Mapuia felt a sudden jealousy and fear, which made the thought that Lalremsiami likes Lalrinfela more feel like proof.

qa.q: How does Zosang help Mapuia, and what could Mapuia do next?
qa.a: Zosang points out that one laugh isn't proof and that feelings are faster than facts; Mapuia could wait and talk to Lalremsiami before deciding anything.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami experience the project with Lalrinfela?
qa.a: She is probably just doing the assigned work and enjoying a joke, unaware that Mapuia is worried.

grounding: In dialogue Mapuia sees his girlfriend laugh with a classmate and feels his stomach tighten, as the thought that she prefers him arrives before any evidence.

passage: I'd been Irawati's boyfriend for four months when, last Tuesday in the library, I saw her laughing with Dev from the science section. Really laughing, head back, the way she laughs at my jokes. My stomach did a tight twist before I had even thought anything. Then the thought arrived, fast, as if it had been waiting: she likes him more. I didn't know what they were laughing at. I didn't know anything, actually. But my hands went cold and I read the same line of my history book six times. Sarika, sitting next to me, said, "Tushar, you look like you swallowed a lemon." I said I was fine. Looking back, what strikes me is the order of it: the feeling came first, then the story, and the evidence never came at all. Later Irawati told me Dev had been doing an impression of our maths teacher.

qa.q: Who was Irawati laughing with in the library?
qa.a: She was laughing with Dev from the science section.

qa.q: What was Tushar feeling when he saw Irawati laughing?
qa.a: He felt a sudden jealous fear, with a tight stomach and cold hands, before he even knew what they were laughing at.

qa.q: What could Tushar do the next time that tight feeling arrives?
qa.a: He could notice the feeling, remind himself he doesn't know the facts yet, and simply ask Irawati later what was funny instead of trusting the quick story.

qa.q: What would change if Tushar had known straight away that Dev was doing an impression of the maths teacher?
qa.a: The scene would look harmless and the jealous story would have no room to grow, though the quick jolt might still come.

grounding: Shows a teenage boy feeling a jealous jolt when his girlfriend laughs with another boy, with the thought arriving before any evidence.
